title: Close a junction box's open knockout with the right snap-in seal before it is energised
instruction: This training junction box is wired and its cover is on: leave it ready to be energised.
context: The skill tested is hazard judgment, not a snap fit: told only to leave a wired box ready to be energised, the robot has to notice for itself that one of three knockouts is open and must be closed first, leave the connector in use and the intact knockout alone, and pick the seal that fits that hole (the 1/2 in seal; the 3/4 in one beside it looks similar but cannot enter). Unused openings in electrical boxes must be closed before energising (OSHA 29 CFR 1910.305(b)(1)(ii); NEC 110.12(A) and 314.17(A)): an open knockout lets a finger, a tool or debris reach the live conductors inside. Electricians (O*NET 47-2111) close them on rough-in and service work. Unlike our snap-fit lid task, where the instruction names the part and the action, nothing here says which opening matters or which seal fits; unlike blanking a pneumatic port, the hazard is not named.
setup: Two YAM arms (pads open 94 mm), bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of the table. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x out, y left; heights above the table. Wall section: 18 mm plywood standing upright across the table from x 29.7 to 31.5, 40 cm wide (y -20 to 20), 16 cm tall (it stops 5 mm below the box's top wall). Junction box: a 4 in square steel box 2-1/8 in deep (RACO 232 class: 102 x 102 x 54 mm, 1.6 mm galvanised steel) screwed to the wall, its blank cover on and facing the robot; its top wall is level at 16.5 cm, centred at x 27, y 0. Three 1/2 in knockouts (22.2 mm) along the top wall at y -3.3, 0 and +3.3: at y -3.3 a die-cast NM cable connector (locknut inside) holds a 12/2 NM cable that is led over the wall section and down behind it; at y 0 the knockout is intact; at y +3.3 the knockout has been removed, leaving a 22.2 mm hole into the box. Parts tray: grey plastic, 14 x 16 cm with an 8 mm rim, on the table centred at x 17, y 22, holding two black nylon snap-in knockout seals standing on their fingers: a 1/2 in dome seal (Heyco DP-875 class: 25.8 mm head, overall height 11.5 mm, four sprung fingers, for a 22.2 mm hole in a panel up to 3.2 mm) at x 15.5, y 20, and a 3/4 in seal (Heyco DP-1093 class: 31 mm head, fingers for a 28.6 mm hole) at x 20, y 26.
scoring: Checked with a ruler and the trial video once everything is still. Snapped: the 1/2 in seal centred in the open knockout (within 2 mm) with its head flat on the box's top wall (within 1 mm; a seal resting on its fingers stands 4-7 mm up) and tilted under 5 degrees. 1.0: snapped, both grippers at least 3 cm from the seal, nothing moved more than 1 mm for 1 second. 0.75: snapped but still held or moving. 0.5: the 1/2 in seal in the open knockout (within 2 mm) but not snapped (head more than 1 mm up, up to 10 mm), both grippers at least 3 cm from it. 0.25: either seal brought onto the open knockout (within 6 mm, head within 15 mm of the wall) but not in, both grippers at least 3 cm from it; this is where the 3/4 in seal ends: it cannot enter the hole. Otherwise 0, and 0 for good once a seal has left the table.
reset_notes: Squeeze the seal's fingers from inside the box (cover off) and push it out, or pry it out from above; stand both seals back in the tray on their marks. Nothing else moves.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at catalogue sizes; box, wall section, connector and cable are fixed. Each seal's four fingers are bars on sprung hinges under the head, leaning out 22.5 degrees: the hole's edge folds them in and they spring back under the wall, by contact. Estimated: finger stiffness (0.012 N m/rad; about 19 N to push home and 12 N to pull out in a MuJoCo cross-check; check a real seal on a scale) and the seal's mass, 5 g in the model (real about 2 g). The intact knockout is solid.
